data.name: Amruta
data.gender_notes: Amruta is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Amruta is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘amrutam’ which means ‘nectar’ or ‘immortality’. In Hindu mythology, Amruta is the name of the heavenly drink which grants immortality. The Gods were believed to drink Amruta from the divine cow Kamadhenu. The name Amruta carries the meaning “Nectar of immortality” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amruta usually hope their child will grow to embody nectar of immortality and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: May you be blessed with a life filled with divine nectar and eternal happiness.
data.etymology: Amruta belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nectar of immortality.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amruta total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Amruta holds an exquisite cultural significance in Hinduism, symbolizing abundance, prosperity, and unending love. The fluid connotation of the name Amruta is also reflected in various rituals such as the Amruta Kalash, wherein a pot filled with water symbolizing Amruta, is an essential part of many Hindu weddings and auspicious events.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Amruta bestows the blessings of eternal happiness, purity, and divinity. It serves as a constant reminder of the eternal love and devotion towards the gods and the quest for immortality and spiritual growth. The name is believed to bring peace, prosperity, and good fortune, making it a cherished and revered identity for an individual.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amruta symbolizes the divine nectar of immortality and eternal bliss in Hinduism. It represents the pure, elixir-filled stream of consciousness, nourishing the soul and sustaining its spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Amruta River is mentioned in ancient Hindu scriptures like the Mahabharata and Rigveda. It is considered one of the sacred rivers in Hinduism, flowing through the North Western region of India.
The name 'Amruta' is also given to a queen in Indian mythology, who was the wife of King Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata epic. She is known for her exceptional beauty and grace.

modern_usage.modern_context: Amruta, a Sanskrit name meaning 'nectar of the gods,' is increasingly popular on social media and wellness platforms. On Instagram, you can find numerous accounts dedicated to Hindu mythology and spirituality where Amruta is used as a hashtag (#Amruta) to explore related content. Pinterest boards and blogs showcase Amruta as a name for products and services such as Ayurvedic skincare, yoga and meditation classes, and even spiritual retreats. The name carries a sense of spiritual nourishment, transcendence, and connection to the divine.
